questions.q: 12 customers with missing spend churned at 41.7% versus 19.3% for the rest. What is the right interpretation?
options: Missing spend causes churn
Twelve customers is far too few to conclude anything; note it, handle it, and check the choice does not matter
The dataset is invalid and must be discarded
The 19.3% figure must be wrong
questions.explain: With only 12 rows, one customer moves the rate by more than 8 points. We fill with plan medians and confirm dropping the rows gives nearly the same ticket results.

questions.q: Why did the lesson re-run the ticket comparison after dropping the 12 rows?
options: To make the dataset smaller
Because dropping rows is always better than filling
To confirm the missing-data handling choice does not drive the result
To remove the baseline
questions.explain: The rates (11.0, 14.7, 26.1, 43.6 percent) were nearly identical to the filled version, so the choice does not matter here.

questions.q: Region gave a chi-square p-value of 0.037 after checking four variables. What is the most sensible reading?
options: Region definitely drives churn
Region is irrelevant and can never matter
The test is broken because p is below 0.05
Weak evidence: barely under 0.05 while scanning several variables, so treat it as a lead and check new data
questions.explain: When you scan many variables some cross the line by luck. Here the generator gives region no role, a live demonstration of chance.

questions.q: What did crossing tickets with tenure show?
options: Churn rises with tickets within every tenure band and falls with tenure within every ticket group, so the effects add up
Tickets and tenure cancel each other out
Only new customers are affected by tickets
Tenure had no relationship to churn
questions.explain: Even for 37-60 month customers, 3+ tickets meant about 32% churn versus 5% with none.

questions.q: In the pivot table, the 25-36 month, 3+ ticket cell has only 13 customers. How should you treat it?
options: As the most important number in the table
As proof of causation
Loosely; read the overall pattern rather than individual small cells
Delete it from the analysis
questions.explain: Small cells are noisy. The overall pattern across bands is more trustworthy than any single small cell.
